Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary For tips on how to play Perudo, see Tips_dudo Contents 1 Attention! 2 Goal of the Game 3 Setup 4 Playing a round 4.1 Calling Dudo 4.2 Increasing the bid 4.3 Palifico 5 Optional rules 5.1 Calza 5.2 Lost dice are visible Attention! There are a lot of variations of Perudo. The variation implemented on BGA is the Asmodée version. Unfortunately, for this version of the game there seems to be no online English rule book. The link on the game page links to another version of Perudo and consequently it discusses rules that are not implemented on this BGA version. Goal of the Game Be the last player remaining with at least 1 die in play. Setup # players 2 3 4 5 6 # dice 10 15 20 25 30 Each player starts with five standard six sided dice, with numbers 1-6. A ​ is known as a " Paco ". A Paco can count as any die value . On BGA, Pacos are depicted as birds on the '1' side of each die. Playing a round All players roll their dice, and check to see what they rolled. Each bid takes into account all of the dice on the table. A player starts with an opening bid of both: A die value and A number of dice. Play passes to the next player on the left, who must then either: Increase the bid or Call Dudo ("I doubt") Always results in a player losing a die. The player that loses a die starts the next round. If this player has only one die left, it triggers a Palifico round . When a player loses their last die, that player is out of the game. The next round begins with the player to the left of the eliminated player. Note: An opening bid can never begin with a bid of Pacos, unless it is a Palifico round . Calling Dudo As soon as Dudo is called all players reveal their dice. All dice that match the bid are counted, including Pacos. Unless it is a Palifico round . If the number of dice is lower than the bid, the player who made the last bid loses one die. If the number of dice is higher or the same as the bid, the player who called Dudo loses one die. Example 1 ​ Amy bids 4 ​ Bob calls " Dudo ". All the dice are revealed and counted up: ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ 2 ​ + 2 Pacos ( ​ ) = 4 ​ Bob loses a die . Example 2 ​ Amy bids 1 Paco ( ​ ). Bob calls " Dudo ". All the dice are revealed and counted up: ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Only Pacos ( ​ ) count. Amy loses a die . Increasing the bid If a player does not want to call Dudo, they must make a higher bid of their own, at least one of: Increase the number of dice (with any die value) e.g. increase a bid of 5 ​ to 6 ​ . Increase the die value (if possible) e.g. increase a bid of 5 ​ to 5 ​ . Increase the bid to a Paco die value. The number of Pacos must be at least half the number of dice rounded up. e.g. increase a bid of 5 ​ s to 3 Pacos ( ​ ). Increase the bid from a Paco die value. The number of dice must be at least double the number of Pacos + 1. e.g. increase a bid of 3 Pacos ( ​ ) to 7 ​ . Palifico The moment a player has only one die remaining, this player has reached "Palifico". Pacos no longer count as any die value An opening bid can be any die value, including Pacos. The die value cannot be changed. After this round, the game resumes as normal, regardless of whether the Palifico player still has one die left. Optional rules Calza Any player except the player who made the current bid can call Calza. As soon as Calza is called all players reveal their dice. All dice that match the bid are counted, including Pacos. If the number of dice is exactly the same as the bid, the player who called Calza gains one die. If the player only had one die, then the next time they fall to having only one die will not trigger another Palifico round . If the number of dice is not the same as the bid, the player who called Calza loses one die. If the player who called out Calza has at least one die, they begin the new round. [Rating: 1/10] 06/10/01 Almost mindless dice rolling. Made Yahtzee seem sophisticated. Played once, hated it (maybe because I was sober).

[Rating: 1/10] I Haaattteee this game.  i do not like bluffing  and bidding games expecially with small amounts of info and this is what this game is.  However I have nuemrous copies of most versions of this gaem including perudo.

[Rating: 1/10] What a terrible excuse for a game. How about I think of a number, 1-50, and you wager against other people what I picked. Also, this is going to take, like, 20 minutes.   Awful concept that requires exactly zero strategy or skill. 0/10.

[Rating: 1/10] I will leave the house in order to avoid having to listen to the cacophony of those hard, clunky dice rattling around in those hard, clunky cups.  The gameplay is also offensive to me, but I might find it occasionally enjoyable (in a somewhat psychologically unhealthy way), if it were played with more tolerable components (compare with Roll for the Galaxy's softer cups and tiny, round-cornered dice).

[Rating: 1/10] I disdain Push-Your-Luck mechanics in general, this distills it down to it's worst components to make it awful and bland and then throws in bluffing to boot... hard pass.

[Rating: 1/10] "Played" on BGA. I had NO clue what I was doing the entire game. I randomly chose dice and values without any idea of what to do.

[Rating: 1/10] No Cards. It's pretty basic, not much going on here. Would rather just play Farkle or Yahtzee.

[Rating: 1/10] Awful "game" that rarely classifies as a game. Liar's Dice is basically guess work and hoping one guess right. Liar's Dice is like the game Guess Who in that sense, but with less skill. It's almost impossible to know when someone is lying or not, especially with more players. Liar's Dice is a luck randomfest. I like bluffing games, but I prefer bluffing games with a way to deduce when people are lying or not with some intelligence, and there seems to be very little of it here. I played a bunch on BGA to give the game a fair chance and I hate it each time.
